questions.q: What is the very first diagnostic question to ask when someone reports "I can't do X" in the database?
options: Has the table been backed up recently?
Is the database using PAGE or ROW compression?
What version of SQL Server is being used?
Can the user connect to the server/database at all, or does the connection succeed but this specific action is blocked?
questions.explain: Login/authentication problems and permission problems have completely different causes and fixes, so splitting on this question first avoids wasting time debugging the wrong layer.

questions.q: Which system view lists every user or role that exists inside a database, as a security principal?
options: sys.partitions
sys.dm_exec_connections
sys.dm_os_wait_stats
sys.database_principals
questions.explain: sys.database_principals is the starting point for confirming a security principal actually exists in the database before investigating its permissions further.

questions.q: Why is fn_my_permissions a more reliable answer than manually adding up GRANTs and role memberships?
options: It returns the principal's effective permissions, already accounting for role membership and any DENY that might override a grant
It ignores DENY statements entirely
It only works for sysadmin accounts
It automatically fixes any missing permissions it finds
questions.explain: fn_my_permissions computes the actual, effective result across every path — direct grants, roles, and DENY — instead of requiring you to trace each path by hand.

questions.q: According to the troubleshooting methodology in this lesson, what should be checked before diving into explicit grants and role memberships?
options: The number of partitions on the affected table
That the connection itself succeeds, and that the security principal exists where expected
The database's current compression settings
The most recent backup's completion time
questions.explain: The methodology starts by confirming the connection works and that the principal exists in sys.database_principals, before investigating explicit grants, roles, or DENY.

questions.q: What comes next after Chapter 4 closes, according to this lesson?
options: The final DP-300 exam review chapter
A repeat of Chapter 4's authentication topics
Chapter 5, Azure SQL Network Security — firewalls, virtual networks, and private connectivity
Chapter 14, High Availability & Disaster Recovery
